reviews.text: I read a previous client's comment. The doctor treats senior dogs with great dedication and extreme sensitivity. The problem arises when clients aren't willing to follow the necessary procedures for seniors, such as repeated tests to determine any worsening conditions and medication changes, which can, however, worsen the situation. Furthermore, consultations and medications are often requested ONLY over the phone, without monitoring critically ill patients...which, of course, aren't prescribed to avoid an irreversible worsening of the situation.

Unfortunately, I can't give zero stars.
The doctor practically abandoned me with a 16-year-old patient who was terribly ill. She didn't want to take the responsibility of giving him medicine, and so from one day to the next she stopped responding. To be a good doctor, you need to have a lot of humanity first and foremost, and empathize with a dog owner who needs help. Instead, sometimes her responses made me feel like I was bothering her just because I was desperate and needed her help.
My 16-year-old dog isn't well. He has several tumors and cries from morning to night. All I asked for was something to ease the pain and calm him down! But the doctor told me there was nothing I could give him other than supplements. I did, and gave them to him for a month, but they didn't help! So I turned to another specialist who was able to give me medicine to make him feel better... so my experience is absolutely negative. If you have dogs with trivial problems you will be fine, but if your dog is as bad as mine, it is likely that you too will be abandoned!
